svg.title: When your balance senses lie
svg.desc: Four illusions. The leans: after a slow, unnoticed roll and a quick correction you feel banked the opposite way when level. Somatogravic: forward acceleration on a dark take-off feels like a nose-up pitch, and pushing forward flies into the ground. Graveyard spiral: the canals adapt to a sustained turn, the wings feel level, and pulling back tightens the spiral. Autokinetic: a single light stared at in darkness appears to move. In every case, believe the instruments.
svg.text: slow roll, then a quick correction
danger: leaning into a bank, a spiral
danger: pushing forward into the ground
inner ear adapts to a sustained turn
danger: the pull tightens the spiral
staring at a single light in darkness
a star or a lone light
feels: the light drifts and moves
danger: chasing a star as if an aircraft
The attitude indicator will disagree with your senses, and the senses
feel completely convincing. Keep head movements small; don't stare at single lights.
